goal: Pose the question "What does a healthy body and mind need every day?" and sort pictured actions under body, mind or friends, ending with one choice and a reason.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1. Picture sort on paper (optional one-screen version, paper beside it). Unit home task goes home: a talk with a trusted adult the child chooses (a school adult counts), English and Spanish. The body-names family note goes home this week (English and Spanish): the words first, no pictures, preview offered, a quiet opt-out of that one part of day 3; marked "person read before publishing" (later.csv L89). Words only; no body-size talk.

goal: Teach hand washing in five pictured steps with the step card (why, the steps, the teacher model, every child washes at the sink, feedback) and the moments it matters, and say who it protects.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO5. Fact: scrub while singing a short song twice, about 20 seconds (CDC "Clean Hands", source and year confirmed at the expert read). Supplies: fragrance-free school soap and paper towels from school stock; the class sink; wipe spills at once (slips); five minutes of the period kept for washing and drying. A child without soap at home is never singled out; school does the doing. Self-check 1 of 2: face card on the washing steps. Safety agent read (sink).

goal: Name outside body parts and the main inside parts, and say the private part names once in a calm voice with the idea of private; pairs then hold the washing card for a five-minute rehearsal.
note: PERSON READ BEFORE PUBLISHING (later.csv L89): this day and its family note. Sensitivity flag: body names (sensitivity read with docs/reviews/sensitivity-health-body-names-2026-11-20.md and a national pediatrics association family page). Week 3, two weeks after the family note; a child kept out of this part by the family does the washing rehearsal with another adult. Words only: no pictures, diagrams, body outlines or pointing; nothing about what parts do; private part words are penis, vulva, breasts and bottom. A question gets one calm sentence and the class moves on. If a child says anything about being touched or hurt: listen, do not promise secrecy, do not question, follow the school duty to report. No later item, check or task asks a child to say the private part names.

goal: Teach why sleep and rest help a body and mind grow, and build a calm bedtime routine as a picture list; wash before snack without the card.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO2. Candidate kept (0 days added): "brush teeth" is one picture in the bedtime routine list, if the HECAT PHW PreK-2 read lists a dental expectation; otherwise the picture stays as a routine step only. Never ask about a child's bedtime or how long they sleep; the routine is a character's. The washing card is withdrawn today (first use without it). Self-check 2 of 2: face card on the washing steps.

goal: End-of-unit check on unseen pictured cards read aloud: order the washing steps, pick a moment to wash and say who it protects, sort an action under body, mind or friends, one facts-in-use item on sleep, and a valuing item on a character who skips washing.
note: Each child answers alone by circling, drawing, pointing or telling an adult who scribes (about 15 minutes); scored on the steps with a guide, met, partly or not yet. Valuing scored on whether the reason uses a unit fact, never on the choice. No item on body names. Response: the last five minutes re-rehearse the step most often marked not yet; each child's not-yet steps return on the mid-year respond day.

goal: Pose the question "What helps my body grow and feel strong?" and name foods that help us grow and foods to have less often, by color, on a pictured plate.
note: HECAT.FN.HBO1, HBO2, HBO3. Candidate kept (0 days added): one sentence on noticing hungry and full, if the HECAT FN PreK-2 read lists it; breakfast is left to unit 8 (its own Candidate). Sensitivity flag: food. Never ask what a child eats at home; "by color" means a rainbow of fruit and vegetable colors on the plate, with no red, yellow or green food labels; no good or bad foods, no weighing, no calories. Optional tasting of two fruits or vegetables ($15 for 30) only under the school food and allergy rules, allergies checked first; otherwise pictures. Unit home task goes home. Safety agent read (tasting).

goal: Teach that water is the drink bodies need most and sweet drinks are for sometimes; children notice thirst and fill a water bottle or cup.
note: HECAT.FN.HBO6, HBO7. Retrieval (5 minutes): which bedtime picture from unit 1 helps the body rest, as water helps it stay strong. Never ask what a child drinks at home; drinks vary by home and budget.

goal: Show that playing hard makes the heart beat faster, with short active bursts in the classroom, a hand on the chest and a water break.
note: HECAT.PA.HBO1, HBO4. PE lean, if later: PE unit 6 (kindergarten weeks 24 to 27) comes later, so this day says the heart fact itself and PE builds on it; health teaches why and the habit, PE the moving. Space: desks pushed back, arms-length spacing, no running between desks; no equipment. A child who cannot run takes part by moving arms or clapping. Safety agent read (active play).

goal: Teach the influence check with the teacher model (name it, helps or hurts, say one why) and sort pictured things (sleep, washing, play, too much sun, foods) into helps or hurts.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO5. Retrieval (5 minutes): the washing steps and the bedtime list from unit 1 are the first "helps" cards. Foods sort as foods that help us grow and foods to have less often, never good or bad. Helps-or-hurts sort on paper first. Self-check 1 of 2: face card on the influence check.

goal: Teach goal step 1 with the teacher model: pick one healthy habit from the class safe list, draw it and say why it helps; pairs hold the influence card for a five-minute rehearsal.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO5. Safe list: washing, water, a sleep routine, time outside. Never about weight, body or food limits; a character's habit is always an option; the drawing stays with the child. Shared goal steps card (SEL STANDARD section 7), kindergarten form "my goal and one step": the habit is "my goal". SEL kindergarten unit 6 (weeks 27 to 32) uses the same card later. Self-check 2 of 2. Last rehearsal before the check: pairs rehearse with the card turned over.

goal: End-of-unit check on unseen pictured cards: sort helps or hurts with one why, pick a habit for a character and say why it helps, facts-in-use items on water, growing foods and a faster heart, and a valuing item.
note: Read aloud; each child answers alone (circle, draw, point or tell an adult). Taken without the influence card, which was turned over in day 10's rehearsal. Response: last five minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the mid-year respond day (week 13).

goal: Kindergarten mid-year check (week 12) on unseen pictured cards: order the washing steps and pick a moment, sort an action under body, mind or friends, pick the one picture that hurts and say why, and match a habit to a character.
note: Course-level check right after unit 2's end: its items on unit 2's skills are drawn from unit 1's habits (washing, sleep) in a pick-one form, not day 11's sort, and unit 2's end record is carried, not re-scored. No item on body names. Each part of each code gets its own short prompt.

goal: Respond: groups from the class record sheet re-rehearse each "not yet" step on a new scenario.
note: Groups from the record sheets of units 1 and 2 and the mid-year check; each "not yet" step re-rehearsed on a scenario not used before.

goal: Pose the question "What can I do with a big feeling, and how do I show I am listening?" and teach the I-statement "I feel ___ when ___. I need ___." with the teacher model on a character scene.
note: HECAT.MEH.HBO1, HBO2. SEL lean: SEL kindergarten unit 2 (weeks 5 to 10) has taught the feeling faces, so they open as a five-minute retrieval; where the school does not run SEL, the first ten minutes teach the four faces. One feelings faces chart shared with SEL. Feelings are a character's; no child is asked about feelings at home. A child who does not speak points to a face card. Unit home task goes home.

goal: Use the shared calm-down card, "stop, breathe" with the slow balloon breath, practiced while calm, and choose when a character would use it; pairs hold the I-statement card for five minutes.
note: HECAT.MEH.HBO5, HBO7. SEL lean: SEL kindergarten unit 2 teaches the card first; health uses that card, word for word (SEL STANDARD section 7), not its own. Where the school does not run SEL, the first ten minutes teach the card. A calm-down tool is never a punishment. Self-check 1 of 2: face card on the I-statement.

goal: Teach listening in four pictured steps (look, quiet body, wait, say back) with the teacher model, then with a partner who is different from me, in the class circle and in a lunch table or playground scene.
note: HECAT.MEH.HBO4. The SEL talk turn card's two steps, "eyes look, wait my turn" (SEL kindergarten unit 1), open the listening card (SEL STANDARD section 7). Scenes vary characters in family, ability and culture.

goal: Teach kind words and gentle hands: unkind acts hurt and an adult can help; pairs rehearse the listening card turned over (the last rehearsal before the check); a third of the class says the I-statement for a character.
note: HECAT.V.HBO1, HBO3. Candidate kept (0 days added): one scene on showing care for a character's feelings, inside this day. Said-aloud record: ten children heard (about a minute each) on the class record sheet while the others draw a kind act; the rest on day 18. Bullying roles are out (grade 3). Self-check 2 of 2. The observation records NHES.S4.2.1 only (the I-statement); kind words and gentle hands (NHES.S4.2.5) are taught today and assessed on days 18 and 27.

goal: End-of-unit check: the rest of the class says the I-statement for a character; every child answers unseen pictured scenes (show or say one kind thing to do for a character, pick a calm tool for a character, a listening step in two pictured places, the class circle and the lunch table, with a prompt for each), with a facts-in-use item and a valuing item.
note: Pictured scenes read aloud first (about 12 minutes); then the teacher hears the I-statement at a side table while the class draws, and in the same minute reads the child one line and marks "says back" for the listening step; any child not heard in the period is heard that week in the classroom routine (health is the classroom teacher's course), on the same sheet. Pointing to face cards counts. Response: last minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the year-end respond day. The kind thing may be said, pointed to or acted with a puppet (NHES.S4.2.5 asks for acting with care, not picking).

goal: Pose the question "Who helps keep me safe, and what do I do when I have a choice?" and teach the two signs of a trusted adult (keeps you safe, listens) with help step 1, sort pictured adults by them and model the ask "Can you help me?".
note: HECAT.S.HBO4, HBO5. Children choose some of their own helpers on a hand drawing; families vary, and a school adult always counts. SEL lean: SEL kindergarten unit 1 (weeks 1 to 4) named school helpers by picture; health adds home and nearby helpers and the two signs. SEL unit 5 (weeks 20 to 25) runs alongside with "No, I don't want to". Unit home task goes home.

goal: Pairs hold the help card and rehearse "Can you help me?" for characters in scenes from days 19 and 14 to 18, using the I-statement words for what to say.
note: Practice only: every step and line was modeled on day 19 and in unit 3. The ask previews NHES.S8.2.1 (owned in grade 1 unit 7), begun here (~ in codes), not claimed. Retrieval (5 minutes): the I-statement from unit 3. Self-check 1 of 2: face card on the help step.

goal: Teach decision step 1 with the teacher model: stop and say "I have a choice", on pictured scenes including crossing a street with a grown-up.
note: HECAT.S.HBO1, HBO3. Candidate settled (0 days added): street crossing kept as one scene here; "know my address" dropped, because a task on a child's home address asks about home, which this course never does, and the school holds that record.

goal: Teach that seat belts, car seats and helmets lower the chance of getting hurt, show a helmet fitted on a doll, and use "I have a choice" on gear scenes.
note: HECAT.S.HBO3, HBO7. Supplies: one child's helmet and a doll, borrowed (or $15 for a helmet); fitted on the doll or on a partner's own school helmet only, never shared between heads. Car-seat fitting is out. Source: the national highway traffic safety agency car seat and booster pages (browser check, For the lead). Safety agent read. Begins NHES.S1.2.3 (owned in grade 1 unit 6).

goal: Teach "leave it and tell": medicine only from a trusted grown-up, pills and cleaners left alone, smoke and vapor are not good for lungs, and the norm "most grown-ups do not smoke or vape"; sort leave-it-and-tell pictures without the card.
note: HECAT.AOD.HBO1; T.HBO1, HBO2; S.HBO1. Norm in plain words, no figure (CDC adult tobacco use pages, source and year at the expert read). Pictures only: no real medicine, cleaner, cigarette, vape or lighter. A child who lives with someone who smokes is never made to feel blame for that person. Poison Help page: browser check. Unit 5 family note and leave-out note go home this week (two weeks before week 25). Self-check 2 of 2. Begins NHES.S1.2.3 (owned in grade 1 unit 6).

goal: End-of-unit check on unseen pictured scenes: point to a helper for each and to the sign card that shows why they are trusted, spot the choice, pick "leave it and tell", with facts-in-use items on gear, medicine and smoke and a valuing item.
note: Read aloud; each child answers alone. Response: last five minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the year-end respond day.

goal: Pose the question "What do I do if a touch does not feel safe?" and teach in simple words: my body is mine, some touches are safe and some are not, secrets about touch are never kept, tell a trusted adult until one helps.
note: SENSITIVE (body safety), removable: leave-out note on the first page; the longer family note (English and Spanish) went home in week 23 with the outline and how to opt out through the school (at home the parent decides). HECAT.V.HBO8. Practices NHES.S3.2.1 (unit 4) and begins NHES.S4.2.3 (grade 1 unit 7); claims no code. Candidate kept (0 days added): "surprises are okay, secrets about touch are not" is part of this day. No child is asked about their own experience; no role play of a person who touches. If a child tells: listen, do not promise secrecy, follow the school duty to report, tell the child who the next adult is; a parent at home is pointed to the national child abuse hotline by purpose. Sensitivity read with the sources named in the frame. A child whose family opted out does a help-steps picture sort with another adult.

goal: Rehearse the telling line from a written script with a card playing any pressure, then the end-of-unit check on unseen pictured scenes: point to "tell" and to a helper.
note: SENSITIVE (body safety). Scripts of the telling line only; the teacher or a card plays any pressure. Scored on the help steps; practiced NHES.S3.2.1 is not claimed. Disclosure steps as on day 25.

goal: Kindergarten year-end check (week 27) on unseen pictured cards: the I-statement and a listening step for a character in two pictured places (the class circle and the lunch table, a prompt each), show or say one kind thing to do for a character (said, pointed or acted with a puppet), a helper and one sign card, spot a choice, with one item each from units 1 and 2.
skills: k-meh-feeling-words; k-meh-good-listening; k-v-kind-words-and-hands; k-s-trusted-helpers; k-s-notice-a-choice; k-phw-hand-washing; k-phw-things-that-help
codes: NHES.S4.2.1; NHES.S4.2.2; NHES.S4.2.5; NHES.S3.2.1; NHES.S5.2.1; NHES.S7.2.1; NHES.S2.2.1
note: Pointing to faces counts for the I-statement. Unit 3's said-aloud record is carried, not re-heard. Carried items: order the washing steps (NHES.S7.2.1); helps or hurts with one why (NHES.S2.2.1). Never unit 5, so leaving unit 5 out changes nothing here.

goal: Respond: groups from the record sheets re-rehearse each "not yet" step on a new scenario.
note: Groups from units 3 and 4 and the year-end check.

goal: Pose the question "How do I keep germs from spreading, and what am I already good at?" and name a strength for body, mind and friends that keeps me healthy; start the daily-habits picture chart.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO2. Retrieval (5 minutes): sort one action under body, mind or friends (kindergarten unit 1). Strengths are actions (washing, trying foods, asking for help, being kind), never body traits. The habits chart is kept a week by the child's choice, stays with the child and is never scored. Doing record for NHES.S7.2.2 starts: across the unit the teacher marks each child carrying out the taught routines at school (washing before snack and using their own cup, every day; coughing into the elbow marked when seen, not required), met, partly or not yet on the steps. Unit home task goes home.

goal: Teach that germs are too small to see and some can spread from person to person and make people sick, show it with the teacher's washable-paint handshake, and teach the cough-and-wash card with the teacher model and pair practice.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO3. Retrieval (5 minutes): the kindergarten washing steps and the bedtime list. Habits: wash, cough into the elbow, stay home when sick, do not share cups. Supplies: washable paint (teacher only), soap and towels; five minutes for washing and clean-up. No blame for who gets sick; no illness stories. Self-check 1 of 2. Safety agent read (paint, hand washing).

goal: Teach how to protect eyes, ears and skin (hats, shade, sunglasses, sunscreen put on by an adult, turning sound down), state the class norm from the routine record, and pairs hold the cough-and-wash card.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO4, HBO5. Retrieval (5 minutes): outside body names only (eyes, ears, skin) from kindergarten unit 1, matched to a protection. Norm from the teacher's own routine record, "most of our class covered a cough this week", never naming a child. Candidate kept (0 days added): one sentence that school hearing and vision checks help, if the HECAT PHW read lists it. No sunscreen product is handled by children. Self-check 2 of 2. Last rehearsal before the check: pairs rehearse with the card turned over.

goal: End-of-unit check on unseen pictured scenes: pick the germ-stopping action and say why, match a body part to its protection, point to one strength card that is yours (the cards are safe actions only) and a strength for a character, a facts-in-use item and a valuing item; the routine record goes into the judgment for NHES.S7.2.2.
note: NHES.S7.2.2 is judged on the routines every child does daily (washing before snack, own cup); cough covering is marked when seen, not required. It is judged from the teacher's record of each child doing the routines at school, never from a character's chart and never on health or home habits. Response: last five minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the mid-year respond day.

goal: Pose the question "When something feels wrong, who do I tell and what do I say?" and teach the help steps (say who you need, what happened, that it matters) with the teacher model.
note: HECAT.S.HBO4, HBO5. Retrieval (5 minutes): name two helpers on the kindergarten helper hand. Scenes are characters'; no child is asked about their own worries or family. SEL lean: SEL grade 1 unit 9 (weeks 10 to 15) uses the same help-step words after this unit. Unit home task goes home.

goal: Teach asking a trusted adult for help with a worry that will not go away, with the I-statement "I feel ___ when ___. I need ___." (need: help), and listening to what the adult says.
note: HECAT.MEH.HBO4. Retrieval (5 minutes): the I-statement and listening cards from kindergarten unit 3, back for this one day. The worry scene also practices the help steps, so standard 3 is met in mental health as well as safety. Self-check 1 of 2.

goal: Teach what to say or do when something feels wrong or unsafe: say stop, say it again, move away, tell, and keep telling, on scenes of a rough game, a stranger asking for something, a scary place and an online ask.
note: HECAT.S.HBO6, HBO7; V.HBO7. Refusal second push in the shared words (SEL STANDARD section 7): say it again, move away, tell. Candidate kept (0 days added): the online-ask scene. An adult plays any pressure from a script; no child plays the person. Stranger scenes stay calm, with no kidnapping detail.

goal: Teach decision step 2 (does this choice need a grown-up?) with the teacher model, the people who give medicine safely and why we ask first, and "leave it, tell" for a found vape or pills.
note: HECAT.AOD.HBO1; S.HBO5. Retrieval (5 minutes, one opening picture, not three tasks): "I have a choice: leave it and tell", which brings back noticing a choice, medicine only from a trusted grown-up and staying away from smoke and vapor (all kindergarten unit 4). Pictures only. Never test knowledge of home medicines. SEL lean: SEL grade 1 unit 9 uses class choices after this; health owns the safety topics. Self-check 2 of 2.

goal: Pairs rehearse with the help card turned over (the last rehearsal before the check) the help request for characters on scenes from days 33 to 36; a third of the class says the request to the teacher.
note: Practice only, no new content. Said-aloud record: ten children heard with the card turned over, as on day 38, on the class record sheet while the others draw the helper they would ask; the rest on day 38. The observation records the help request only (NHES.S3.2.2 and NHES.S8.2.1); pairs also rehearse the feels-wrong steps from day 35, practice not recorded here.

goal: End-of-unit check without the card: the rest of the class says the help request for a character; every child answers unseen pictured scenes (who to ask and what to say, what to do when something feels wrong, alone or ask a grown-up), with a facts-in-use item on medicine and a valuing item.
note: Pictured scenes first, then the side-table hearing; any child not heard is heard that week in the classroom routine. Response: last minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the mid-year respond day.

goal: Grade 1 mid-year check (week 11) on unseen pictured scenes: a germ-stopping action and why, one "hurt" prompt (a helmet or sun scene: what lowers the chance of getting hurt?), point to one strength card that is yours and a strength for a character, what to say when something feels wrong, who to ask and what to say, alone or ask a grown-up.
skills: g1-phw-stop-germs; g1-phw-my-strengths; g1-s-unsafe-feels-wrong; g1-s-ask-for-help; g1-meh-tell-a-helper; g1-s-choose-and-ask
codes: NHES.S1.2.3; NHES.S1.2.1; NHES.S4.2.3; NHES.S3.2.2; NHES.S8.2.1; NHES.S5.2.2
note: Course-level check right after unit 7's end: its items on unit 7's skills use unit 6's scenes (a classmate who feels sick, a shared cup) in a pointing form, so they do not repeat day 38. Unit 7's said-aloud record (days 37 and 38, inside ten days) is carried, not re-heard. NHES.S7.2.2 comes from unit 6's routine record, carried, not re-scored.

goal: Respond: groups from the record sheets re-rehearse each "not yet" step on a new scenario.
note: Groups from units 6 and 7 and the mid-year check.

goal: Pose the question "What around me helps me be healthy, and how do I choose a snack?" and teach how the places we live and learn affect health, and how a clean, safe shared place helps everyone who uses it.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO5. Retrieval (5 minutes): the kindergarten helps-or-hurts sort, influence card back for this one day. Children draw a healthy place of their own choice, never their own home. Unit home task goes home.

goal: Teach the second part of the influence check, say how it touches me, with the teacher model on character scenes (a late night makes a character tired).
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1. Retrieval (5 minutes): why sleep helps, from the kindergarten bedtime list. Scenes are characters'. Self-check 1 of 2.

goal: Use the influence check without the card on a pictured plate with a water cup and on a snack ad invented for practice: what does the ad want, and how could it touch a character?
note: HECAT.FN.HBO1, HBO2, HBO6, HBO7. Retrieval (5 minutes): foods that help us grow and water first (kindergarten unit 2). Pressure met here (bar criterion 4): what the ad wants. Ads invented for practice, no product names. No good or bad foods.

goal: Teach decision step 3 with the teacher model: name two or three snack options for a character and what could happen with each.
note: HECAT.FN.HBO1, HBO3. Retrieval (5 minutes): decision steps 1 and 2 ("I have a choice", kindergarten unit 4; does it need a grown-up, unit 7). Candidate kept (0 days added): one scene where a character eats breakfast, as a character's choice, if the HECAT FN read lists it; never asking a child about breakfast. Options stay foods that help or foods for sometimes; no scolding. Self-check 2 of 2.

goal: End-of-unit check on unseen pictured cards: name an influence and how it touches a character, then "How could this touch you if it happened?", say how a shared place helps the people who use it (a pictured home, school and street scene, none the child's own, a prompt each), give two options and a result for a character's snack, with a facts-in-use item and a valuing item.
note: Read aloud; each child answers alone. Response: last five minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the year-end respond day.

goal: Pose the question "How can playtime stay safe and fair, and what healthy thing will I work on?" and teach safe active play (space, rules, water, stop when hurt) and settling a small problem with words: "Stop, I don't like that."
note: HECAT.PA.HBO1, HBO6; V.HBO1, HBO3. Retrieval (5 minutes): playing hard makes the heart beat faster, the helmet rule, and kind words and gentle hands (kindergarten units 2, 4 and 3). PE lean, side by side: PE unit 12 (weeks 19 to 22) teaches the heart and counting beats; health says the heart fact in one line and names safe-play rules, a week ahead. Candidate kept (0 days added): one line on warming up before play. Space: a cleared area with cones from PE stock, arms-length spacing; water break; a child who cannot run takes part another way. Safety agent read (active play). Unit home task goes home.

goal: Teach ways to help others make safe choices (remind a friend to buckle up, tell an adult when a friend is hurt), using the help steps to get a friend to a helper.
note: HECAT.S.HBO8; V.HBO7. Retrieval (5 minutes): the kindergarten helper hand. The help steps come from unit 7. Self-check 1 of 2.

goal: Teach the goal frame "I will ___" with the teacher model: a goal from the safe list and why it helps.
note: HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HBO2. Retrieval (5 minutes): the habit each child drew in kindergarten unit 2, or a character's. Safe list only (sleep, water, hand washing, time outside, screen breaks, a kind act, asking for help); a character's goal is always an option. SEL lean: SEL grade 1 unit 12 (weeks 27 to 32) reuses this frame later.

goal: Teach the next goal steps with the teacher model: who can help and two or three steps in order, drawn on the goal frame sheet, with "and when we will check" as the plan's last line.
note: Shared goal steps card (SEL STANDARD section 7), grade 1 form: my goal and one step, then a helper and a check. Uses the help steps from unit 7. The plan stays with the child and goes home with ten weeks of the school year left to try it. Unit 10 family note and leave-out note go home this week (two weeks before week 23). Self-check 2 of 2. Last rehearsal before the check: pairs rehearse with the card turned over.

goal: End-of-unit check: each child shows a goal plan (goal, helper, steps), their own or a character's, scored on the goal-plan steps, plus one unseen scene on helping a friend, a facts-in-use item on safe play and a valuing item.
note: Scored on the steps, never on what the goal is. Response: last five minutes on the step most often not yet; the rest on the year-end respond day.

goal: Pose the question "What if the first grown-up I tell does not help?" and teach, on scenes, whom to tell and what to say when the first adult does not help: keep telling.
note: SENSITIVE (body safety), removable: leave-out note on the first page; family note went home in week 21. HECAT.V.HBO8. Practices NHES.S4.2.3 and NHES.S3.2.2 (unit 7); claims no code. If unit 5 was left out, the first ten minutes give its one idea (my body is mine; secrets about touch are never kept). No child is asked about their own experience; no role play of a person who harms. Disclosure steps as in unit 5. Retrieval (5 minutes, where unit 5 was taught): my body is mine, tell until one helps. A child whose family opted out does a help-steps picture sort with another adult.

goal: Rehearse the keep-telling line from a written script, then the end-of-unit check on unseen pictured scenes: point to the next helper.
note: SENSITIVE (body safety). Candidate kept (0 days added): one scene where a friend tells a character a worry, answered with the telling line. A card plays any pressure.

goal: Pose the question "How do we show respect to every family and every person?" and read aloud a short story with families of many structures.
note: Ordinary unit, the way SEL treats families: no leave-out note and no longer family note. HECAT.SH.HBO2, HBO3. Practices NHES.S4.2.5 (kindergarten unit 3) and NHES.S2.2.2 (unit 8); claims no code. No body, reproduction or relationship-history content. Warm, neutral words; families vary in structure, culture and faith (same-sex parents, kinship and foster families among them); no child describes their own family.
